skills.name: kody-cli-bot-getting-started
skills.description: use this for a Kody CLI bot's first chat with its new owner: collect what setup needs, run kody-cli-setup, and confirm it works
skills.content:
---
name: kody-cli-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  use this for a Kody CLI bot's first chat with its new owner: collect what
  setup needs, run kody-cli-setup, and confirm it works
---
# Getting started (Kody CLI bot)

Open with one line: "I work in your Kody account through the Kody CLI and git: I clone, edit, test, commit, push, and publish your Kody repos and packages."

Say how many questions there are, then ask one per message and wait for each answer:

1. "What is your Kody username, and should I work in your personal org or a team org (which handle)?"
2. Kody connection:
   - If the Kody plugin is connected, say: "I'll mint my own CLI credential through the Kody plugin. You will not need to copy any token." Ask whether a 3-month credential (`lifetime: long`) is OK, and whether I may create new repos and packages (adds `package:create`).
   - If it is not connected, ask the owner to connect the Kody plugin (sign in at https://kody.codes and approve access). Fallback: ask them to have any Kody-connected agent run `cliCredentialBootstrap` with `lifetime: "long"`, then submit only the one-shot `kody_bc_...` code through a masked secret field within 10 minutes. kody.codes has no web page for creating CLI tokens. Never ask for a token in chat. If one is pasted, do not repeat it, and suggest revoking it.
3. "What name and email should my git commits use? The email on your Kody account is best."
4. "Which repos or packages should I start on? (`@owner/name`)"

Then:
- Run the `kody-cli-setup` skill end to end.
- Confirm with `kody status`, `kody whoami`, and `git ls-remote https://kody.codes/@<owner>/<name>.git` for the first repo they named.
- Report: CLI version, active org, token expiry date (owner's time zone), and the repos you can reach. Mention you will remint about every 3 months, and how to revoke (`kody auth remove-git`, or `tokenRevoke`).
- Save the username/org, git identity, and starting repos to memory for later sessions.
- From then on, use `kody-search` and `kody-foundations` before looking things up, and `kody-cli-workflow` for repo work.

skills.name: kody-cli-setup
skills.description: use this for one-time setup of the Kody CLI on this box (install, long-lived token bootstrap, git credential helper, git identity, verify) and when the token nears expiry or git returns 401
skills.content:
---
name: kody-cli-setup
description: >-
  use this for one-time setup of the Kody CLI on this box (install, long-lived
  token bootstrap, git credential helper, git identity, verify) and when the
  token nears expiry or git returns 401
---
# Kody CLI setup

Run once per box, and again when the token nears its 3-month cap.
Never print, echo, or paste a `kody_at_...` or `kody_bc_...` value in chat or logs.

## 1. Install
- Needs Node.js 22 or newer (`node --version`). Older Node fails immediately.
- `npm install -g @kodycodes/cli` then `kody --version`.
- No global install? Use `npx -y @kodycodes/cli@latest <command>` (pin `@latest` so npx does not reuse a stale cache).

## 2. Get a long-lived CLI token (preferred: no human handles a token)
There is no kody.codes web page that creates CLI tokens. Use the Kody plugin (MCP):
1. Call `cliCredentialBootstrap` through the Kody MCP `execute` tool (`kody.cliCredentialBootstrap(...)`) or the `api` tool (operationId `cliCredentialBootstrap`) with:
   `{ "name": "<bot name>-cli", "lifetime": "long", "scopes": ["org:execute","org:read","package:read","package:write","package:execute","token:delete"] }`
   Add `package:create` only if the owner wants you to create new repos or packages. Add `search:read` if you want `kody search` from the CLI. Omit `scopes` to get the default set.
2. It returns a one-shot `bootstrap_code` (`kody_bc_...`, redeemable for 10 minutes) and a `cli_command`. Run it, or:
   `kody auth bootstrap --code '<kody_bc_...>' --lifetime long`
3. The CLI stores the resulting `kody_at_...` itself and never prints it. On headless Linux without a keychain it writes a 0600 file under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/kody` (default `~/.config/kody`).

Fallback when the Kody plugin is not connected: ask the owner to run the same `cliCredentialBootstrap` call from any agent connected to their Kody account, then submit only the `kody_bc_...` code through a masked secret field (never chat). Redeem it within 10 minutes as in step 2.
Last resort (CI style): a token from `tokenCreate` (MCP `api` tool, with `"org_binding": "user"` and `"lifetime": "long"`) kept in the `KODY_API_TOKEN` environment variable, submitted via a masked secret field. Never put it in a command line.

Do not run `kody login` here: it needs a browser callback on this machine.

## 3. Git
- `kody auth setup-git` installs a credential helper for `https://kody.codes` (`credential.https://kody.codes.helper` plus `useHttpPath true`, global git config). It reuses the stored token when that token is user-owned and has `package:read` and `package:write`.
- One setup covers every `https://kody.codes/@owner/name.git` you can access, across all orgs. SSH is not supported.
- Set identity to the owner's Kody account (ask if unknown; never invent an email):
  `git config --global user.name "<name>"` and `git config --global user.email "<kody account email>"`

## 4. Verify
- `kody status`: shows stored token scopes and expiry, never the value.
- `kody whoami`: confirms the token identity and scopes.
- `kody org list --json`, and `kody org use <slug>` or `--org <slug>` / `KODY_ORG` for org-scoped commands.
- `git ls-remote https://kody.codes/@<owner>/<name>.git` on a repo you can read.

## 5. Lifetime, renewal, revoke
- `long` = 14 days idle, 3 months absolute max. Each use slides the idle window, never past the max. `short` = 1 hour idle / 24 hours max.
- Without `kody login`, the git helper cannot remint. When `kody status` shows expiry near, or git returns 401: mint a new code (step 2), redeem it, then rerun `kody auth setup-git`.
- `kody auth remove-git` removes the git helper, revokes the stored token on the server, and deletes it locally.
- `kody logout` clears login and a stored bootstrap token. The owner can also revoke via `tokenList` / `tokenRevoke` (MCP `api` tool).

skills.name: kody-cli-workflow
skills.description: use this for day-to-day work on Kody-hosted repos and packages with git and the Kody CLI: clone, edit, test locally, dev check, commit, push, publish, share
skills.content:
---
name: kody-cli-workflow
description: >-
  use this for day-to-day work on Kody-hosted repos and packages with git and
  the Kody CLI: clone, edit, test locally, dev check, commit, push, publish,
  share
---
# Kody CLI workflow

Requires `kody-cli-setup` done. If git or the CLI returns 401, rerun that skill.

## Addressing
- Remote URL: `https://kody.codes/@<owner>/<name>.git` (`<owner>` is a Kody username or org handle).
- With the helper, git sees live HEAD for repos you can read. Anonymous clones of public packages get the published snapshot only, read-only.
- No access and missing look the same: `404 repository not found`. Read-only access: clone works, push gets `403`.

## Find and inspect
- `kody api packageList --params '{}'` and `kody api repoList --params '{}'` (add `--org <slug>` for a team org).
- Prefer the Kody MCP `search` tool for discovery (see `kody-search`).

## Create (needs `package:create` on the token)
- Plain repo: `kody api repoCreate --params '{"name":"<name>","description":"..."}'`.
- New package: create it with `packageGetGitRemote` and `{"create":true,"kody_id":"@<owner>/<leaf>","description":"<= 200 chars"}`, preferably through the MCP `api` tool, because the CLI prints the result and it includes a short-lived git bearer. Then clone the plain URL.
- A plain repo with a root `package.json` becomes a package only via `repoPromoteToPackage`.

## Edit loop
1. `git clone https://kody.codes/@<owner>/<name>.git && cd <name>` (or `git pull` in an existing clone).
2. Edit. `package.json` is the manifest (`name` is `@owner/leaf`; runtime fields under `kody`).
3. Test locally (Node 22+):
   - `kody dev` serves `kody.app.entry` (default `--target mock`). For agents: `kody dev --json --ready-file .kody-dev.json &`, then `kody dev fetch /path`.
   - `kody execute --target mock --invoke ./<export> --params '{...}'`, then `--target prod`.
   - `kody dev job <name>`, `kody dev webhook <name> --body f.json`, `kody dev emit <event> --body e.json`. Add `--dry-run` to preview.
4. `kody dev check` runs local bundles plus the same server checks publish runs. A pass means publish will not refuse. `--offline` skips the server checks, so that guarantee is gone. `--debug` shows the check call.
5. Commit generated files that exports import (`kody.dev.prebuild` does not run at publish). Gitignore local-only `.kody/mocks.ts` and deps maps.

## Commit and push
- Small focused commits with Conventional Commit messages (`fix: ...`, `feat: ...`). Author is the owner's Kody identity from setup.
- `git push origin HEAD:<default branch>`. Plain repos: push is live immediately. Packages: push moves HEAD only and never auto-publishes.
- Limits: 10 MiB per file at publish, about 32 MiB pack per push, 40 MiB request body. Host big binaries elsewhere and commit a link.
- `503 repository busy, retry`: wait and retry. Non-fast-forward: `git pull --rebase`, then push.

## Publish (packages only)
- `kody package publish @<owner>/<leaf>` (add `--json` for structured output).
- Exit 0: `published`, `already_published`, `dispatched`. For `dispatched`, poll `kody api workflowRunList` and do not republish while it runs.
- Exit 1 (npm-like, message on stderr): `checks_failed` (fix and retry), `locked` or `approval_required` (send the owner the `approval_url`), `not_fast_forward`, plus auth or network errors.
- With `--json`, `sent: false` means safe to retry. `sent: "unknown"` means check `workflowRunList` first. Republishing the same commit is safe.

## Sharing
- `kody package collaborators <pkg>`, `kody package grant <pkg> --user <username> --preset use|contribute|manage`, `kody package revoke ...` (needs `package:manage_access`).

## CLI vs MCP
- Use git plus the CLI for multi-file edits, binary assets, local tests, and publish.
- Use MCP `search` / `execute` for discovery, one-off capability calls, and anything that returns secrets or bearer values you should not print.
- MCP-only lane (no shell): `repoOpenSession`, `repoEditFiles`, `repoRunChecks`, `repoPublishSession`. Do not use `repoRunChecks` on pushed but unpublished HEAD.

skills.name: kody-search
skills.description: use this before looking anything up in Kody: what MCP search covers, how to query it, CLI equivalents, community packages, docs, and when to search vs execute vs api
skills.content:
---
name: kody-search
description: >-
  use this before looking anything up in Kody: what MCP search covers, how to
  query it, CLI equivalents, community packages, docs, and when to search vs
  execute vs api
---
# Kody search

## What MCP `search` covers
- Built-in capabilities (grouped in domains such as `email`, `jobs`, `packages`, `mcp:<server>`).
- Official guides (`guide:<id>`), saved packages and their exports, saved integrations, connected MCP servers, and user secret references (metadata only, never values).
- Ranked query results may also attach relevant personal memories. Entity lookups, domain listings, and broad queries do not.
- Not covered: public community listings (use `communitySearch` / `communityGet`), package-scoped secrets (use `secretList` / `packageGet`), plain repos (use `repoList`). Hidden packages are skipped unless `includeHiddenPackages: true`.

## Query tips
- Use a short task phrase ("send an email", "github pull requests"), not a keyword list. Order matters; trust the top hits.
- A broad or empty query returns a domain index. Drill in with `search({ domain })` or `search({ query, domain })`.
- Open detail with `entity`: `capability:<name>`, `guide:<id>`, `package:<name>`, `package:<name>#<export>`, `package:<name>#README.md`, `mcp-server:<name>`, `secret:<name>`. Up to 10 refs per call.
- Large guides return a table of contents. Open a section with `guide:<id>#<heading-slug>` or lines with `#L120-L160`.
- An exact `@owner/leaf`, package name leaf, package UUID, or a copied package or app URL resolves to that package.
- Reuse the returned `conversationId` on follow-up calls.
- Prefer a matching package export hit over just the package. High-confidence hits include an inlined call contract you can run directly.
- MCP server tools are not listed in unscoped results. Use `search({ entity: "mcp-server:<name>" })`, then call `kody.mcp["<name>"].<tool>(args)` from execute.

## Search vs execute vs api
- `search`: discover and read contracts and guides. No side effects.
- `execute`: run an ES module that calls what search found (`kody.<capability>(...)`, `kody:@owner/pkg/export` imports, `kody.mcp[...]`). Adapt the snippet from capability detail.
- `api`: one Open API operation by `operationId` plus flat `params`. Good for token and repo operations and anything the CLI also exposes.

## CLI equivalents
- `kody search "<query>"` with `--entity`, `--domain`, `--limit`, `--json`. A token-only CLI needs the `search:read` scope, which bootstrap tokens do not get by default, so prefer the MCP tool.
- List your packages and repos: `kody api packageList --params '{}'`, `kody api repoList --params '{}'` (add `--org <slug>`).
- Community: `kody api communitySearch --params '{"query":"..."}'`, `kody api communityGet --params '{...}'`. Open capability detail for exact params first.
- Read source: `git clone https://kody.codes/@<owner>/<name>.git`. Public listings clone read-only without auth.

## Docs
- Index of public docs: https://kody.codes/llms.txt. Each page is markdown at `https://kody.codes/docs/<slug>.md`.
- The same guides load in MCP as `search({ entity: "guide:<id>" })`, for example `guide:open_api`, `guide:local_execute`, `guide:auth_setup_git`.
- Source docs: https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/tree/main/docs.
- API reference: https://api-docs.kody.codes and https://api.kody.codes/openapi.json.

## Habits
- Search before building. Reuse or fork an existing package before writing a new one.
- Search before asking the owner for something Kody may already have (an integration, secret name, or package).
- If nothing matches, rephrase once with different task words, then try a domain listing.

skills.name: kody-foundations
skills.description: use this as the reference for core Kody concepts (orgs, packages, visibility, apps, triggers, credentials, memories, follows, execute, credits) before looking them up
skills.content:
---
name: kody-foundations
description: >-
  use this as the reference for core Kody concepts (orgs, packages, visibility,
  apps, triggers, credentials, memories, follows, execute, credits) before
  looking them up
---
# Kody foundations

Kody is a cloud home for agents. The agent brings the reasoning; Kody holds memory, credentials the agent never reads, packages, and triggers that run with no model in the loop. MCP exposes `search`, `execute`, and `api`. Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/what-is-kody.md

## Orgs and handles
- Everyone has a personal org (slug = username) and can create team orgs. Every resource belongs to one org. Handles are permanent.
- The org is the billing and data boundary. Inside it, grants control access (Owner, Member, outside collaborator).
- One MCP connection binds one org. CLI: `--org <slug>`, `KODY_ORG`, or `kody org use`.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/organizations.md

## Packages
- A package is a git repo with the package extension activated. Plain repos are live at HEAD. Packages run their `published_commit`, which moves only on publish.
- `package.json` is the manifest. `name` is `@owner/leaf` (leaf = URL slug). Key `kody` fields: `description` (max 200 chars), `tags`, `category`, `searchText`, `dependencies`, `credentials`, `app`, `jobs`, `webhooks`, `subscriptions`, `emits`, `retrievers`. `exports` is the import map.
- Durable data: `packageStorage()` from `kody:runtime`.
- Visibility is a repo setting, default private (`packageUpdate` `changes.visibility`). Public means listed on `/community` and `/@username`, with source readable and forkable.
- Internet-visible is a separate app flag (`internet_visible`). It serves the app to the public internet after the owner approves a credential and capability summary. Without it, apps are session-gated. "Make it public" means visibility public only, not internet-visible.
- Imports never cross orgs, even with a grant. Fork the other org's public package into your org and import the fork.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/package-authoring.md, https://kody.codes/docs/package-lifecycle.md, https://kody.codes/docs/package-sharing.md

## Apps
- Declared in `kody.app` (`entry`, optional `client`, `assets`). Served at `https://{username}.kody.run/<package-name>/`, or on verified custom domains. Apps are never served from kody.codes.
- Uncertain: the subdomain for team-org packages (docs only say `{username}`).
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/package-apps.md

## Triggers
- Job: recurring schedule in `kody.jobs`. Each run, including `jobRunNow`, gets a 5-minute budget. `jobUpdate` changes schedule, timezone, enabled, params, `expires_at`.
- Workflow: one-off later or long work via `workflows.create({ runAt })`.
- Webhook: `kody.webhooks` binds a name to an export. Mint with `webhookUrlMint`, register with `webhookUrlApply`. The owner must approve via `approval_url`. URLs are credentials and are never returned to agents.
- Subscription: `kody.subscriptions` for Kody events (for example `repo.pushed`, follow events).
- Inbox: every account has an email address.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/triggers.md

## Credentials and secrets
- Code uses secrets by name. There is no plaintext read. `{{secret:name}}` placeholders in secret-aware `fetch` are filled at the network boundary, over HTTPS, for approved hosts only.
- Kinds: Key, OAuth, MCP server, URL, login, signing. Packages declare needs in `kody.credentials` and use scoped `credential(key)` clients.
- Fill placement per credential: headers (optionally named), query, path, body. New credentials default to headers-only. Today an out-of-placement fill is logged as would-block, not refused.
- Owners enter values through `/connect/secret-set` links, never chat.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/credentials.md, https://kody.codes/docs/secrets.md

## Memories
- Personal-only facts that follow the person across agents and orgs. They surface on ranked search, and on execute when `memoryContext` is passed.
- Always run `metaMemoryVerify` before any write. Keep package state, config, credentials, and shared org knowledge out of memory.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/memory.md, https://kody.codes/docs/agent-guidance.md

## Follows
- `followAdd` / `followList` / `followRemove` on `@handle/name`, choosing `published`, `pushed`, or both. Forking also follows upstream.
- CLI: `kody api followAdd ...` (the CLI help does not list a `kody follow` command).
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/package-subscriptions.md

## Execute
- Hosted: MCP `execute` runs in Kody's sandbox and counts against the org's execute pool.
- Local: `kody execute --local` runs in local workerd (Node 22+, Linux/macOS). Every `kody:runtime` call is proxied and metered, but local CPU is free.
- Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/search-and-execute.md, https://kody.codes/docs/local-execute.md

## Plans and credits
- Execute limits are one pool per org. Pro includes Worker compute and rows read. Past the include, prepaid credits pay until they run out, then usage stops. Free keeps daily and weekly caps. Nobody is invoiced for overage.
- Usage: `/@<slug>/-/usage` or `usageGet`. Docs: https://kody.codes/docs/platform-efficiency.md, https://kody.codes/pricing
